seoTitle: How to Cancel Your Coursera Plus Subscription Fast
metaDescription: Cancel Coursera Plus from your account settings in a few steps so you stop paying for a subscription you no longer need, without losing course access early.
intro: If you've finished what you needed on Coursera Plus, or just want to stop the recurring charge before it renews, canceling only takes a couple of minutes once you know where the setting lives. The control isn't tucked inside general Account settings the way you might expect — it's under Purchases, alongside your billing history, which is a common place people miss on their first attempt to find it. This guide walks through finding that exact screen, reading the renewal details before you cancel so you know exactly what you're giving up and when, and what to check afterward so you're not billed again next cycle by mistake. It's especially useful if you signed up during a free trial to finish a single specialization and don't want that trial quietly rolling into a paid subscription, or if you're a business managing a handful of accounts for short-term employee training and need a clean way to wind them down once the training period ends.

steps.heading: Open your account menu
steps.body: Sign in and click your profile photo in the top-right corner of any Coursera page. The dropdown that appears lists My Learning, My Purchases, Settings, and Log Out — My Purchases is the one that matters here, since that's where subscription billing and cancellation live, separately from the general Account settings page used for things like language or timezone. It's a small distinction but an important one, since looking for cancellation inside Settings instead is exactly where most people get stuck first, clicking through profile, notification, and privacy options without ever finding a billing control because it simply isn't there.

steps.heading: Go to Purchases and review your subscription
steps.body: Click My Purchases and select the Subscriptions tab to see your active plan. A typical entry shows the plan name — Coursera Plus monthly subscription — along with your current billing status spelled out in plain language, such as being on a free trial until a specific date and what you'll be charged when the next billing cycle begins. Read this line carefully before canceling, since it tells you exactly what happens and when if you do nothing, which matters most if you're still inside a free trial window and want to cancel before the first real charge lands rather than after.

image.caption: The Purchases page under Subscriptions, showing the Coursera Plus monthly plan, its free trial end date, the upcoming charge, and the Cancel subscription link beneath it.

steps.heading: Click Cancel subscription
steps.body: Directly beneath the plan details is a Cancel subscription link. Clicking it starts the cancellation flow, which on Coursera is a lightweight, self-serve process rather than one that requires contacting support — you don't need to call anyone, open a chat, or submit a ticket to stop the recurring charge, which is a meaningful difference from some subscription services that make cancellation deliberately harder to find.

steps.heading: Confirm the cancellation
steps.body: Coursera will typically ask you to confirm the change before it takes effect, sometimes with a short prompt about what you'll lose access to or an offer to pause instead of fully canceling. Review these details before finalizing, particularly if you're mid-specialization and might want to pick it back up soon, since a pause or a later resubscribe may suit you better than a full cancellation if you're only stepping away temporarily rather than done with the platform entirely. If you decide to go through with it anyway, the confirmation step is also your last chance to note anything you were relying on the subscription for, like offline downloads or certificate access, so nothing catches you off guard once it lapses.

steps.heading: Check your renewal date and confirmation
steps.body: After canceling, look for a confirmation message on-screen or in your email, and revisit the Purchases page to confirm the subscription now shows as canceled rather than active. Note the date your access actually ends — canceling doesn't cut you off immediately, so you'll typically retain access through the remainder of the period you already paid for or the free trial you were on, which means there's no rush to cram in remaining coursework the same day you cancel.

steps.heading: Watch your billing statement the next cycle
steps.body: As a final check, glance at your bank or card statement around the date your old billing cycle would have renewed, just to confirm no charge went through. This takes thirty seconds and closes the loop completely — if something did slip through despite a successful-looking cancellation, catching it on the next statement rather than months later makes it far easier to get resolved through your bank or Coursera support, since disputing a charge from weeks ago is a much harder conversation than flagging one the same day it posts.

faq.question: Will I lose access to my courses right away if I cancel?
faq.answer: No — canceling stops future billing, but you typically keep access through the remainder of your current billing period or free trial rather than losing it instantly.

faq.question: How do I know the cancellation actually went through?
faq.answer: Look for a confirmation message or email after you complete the cancellation, and double-check that your plan shows as canceled on the Purchases page under Subscriptions.

faq.question: Can businesses managing employee accounts cancel the same way?
faq.answer: Yes, the same Purchases and Subscriptions flow applies whether you're managing your own subscription or one tied to short-term employee training.

faq.question: What if I want to come back to Coursera Plus later?
faq.answer: You can generally resubscribe at any time through the same Purchases area if you decide to return.

faq.question: Where exactly is the cancel option located?
faq.answer: It's under My Purchases > Subscriptions, not the general Account settings page — look for the Cancel subscription link directly beneath your plan details.
